messages.subject: Stacked bars with error_bar: how?
parts:
Hello.

The code below shows my intentions. I would like to have error bars
for each of the stacked bars, but in the plot that I have managed to
produce the "position" of the centre of the error bars is not the
location of the top of each stacked bar.
Is there any way of achieving this?

Many thanks in advance for any help.

Pedro.

library(ggplot2)

stack_code <- factor(rep(c('A','B'),4))
treatment <- factor(rep(c('a','a','b','b'),2))
facet_code <- factor(c(rep(1,4),rep(2,4)))
resp <- c(10,1,12,3,9,2,11,3)
SEM <- rep(0.3,8)
test.data <- data.frame(treatment,stack_code,facet_code,resp,SEM)

p <- ggplot(test.data, aes(fill=stack_code, y=resp, x=treatment))
p1 <- p + geom_bar(stat="identity") + facet_wrap(~facet_code)
p2 <- p1 + geom_errorbar(aes(ymax = resp + SEM, ymin=resp - SEM),
width=0.1)
print(p2)

messages.subject: Re: Stacked bars with error_bar: how?
parts:
Hi:

Let me first point you here:
http://biostat.mc.vanderbilt.edu/wiki/Main/DynamitePlots

Please read the one-page poster linked near the bottom of the page (Poster3.pdf) and the last paragraph at the bottom of the page. This will explain the transformation of your plot I am about to suggest below.

I created a new factor for names of the facets, which should be a little more informative than '1, 2'.

To replace the unnecessary, distracting and visually overpowering bars, we plot points for the (mean) response instead. These points have precisely the same amount of information as the bars, with much less ink expended.

stack_code <- factor(rep(c('A','B'),4))
treatment <- factor(rep(c('a','a','b','b'),2))
facet_code <- factor(c(rep(1,4),rep(2,4)))
resp <- c(10,1,12,3,9,2,11,3)
SEM <- rep(0.3,8)
test.data <- data.frame(treatment, stack_code, facet_code, resp, SEM)

test.data$facet <- factor(rep(c('Facet 1', 'Facet 2'), each = 4))

p <- ggplot(test.data, aes(x = treatment, y = resp, colour = stack_code))
p + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
      geom_errorbar(aes(ymax = resp + SEM, ymin = resp - SEM), width = 0.1, size = 1) +
      facet_wrap(~ facet) +
      scale_colour_manual('Stack code', values = c('A' = 'red', 'B' = 'blue')) +
      xlab('Treatment') + ylab('Response')

The size parameters in geom_point() and geom_errorbar() are chosen to make them stand out a little bit more - the use of more dramatic colors has the same purpose.

HTH,
Dennis
